description: Deterministic actor-output corpus for useful insight generation quality.

fixtures.goal: Reduce repeated transition bounces without weakening the gate.

expected_dimensions.label: Classify bounce as ritual, substantive, hybrid, or unknown.
Replay representative gate transcripts before changing policy.
Expose a numeric budget that fails closed on regression.

actor_outputs.text: Classify the bounce first, then replay representative transcripts before touching gate policy.
Add a numeric regression budget so ritual, substantive, hybrid, and unknown rates fail closed in CI.
Represent bounce_kind and budget_guard facts so Prolog can challenge unknown transitions.
Apply the active-mistake pattern: replay telemetry and make the budget visible before close.

fixtures.goal: Find missing user-story requirements in a machine-learning training plan.

expected_dimensions.label: Require known-at-time temporal split or walk-forward validation.
Probe leakage between feature construction and label time.
Compare against simple baselines and ablations.

actor_outputs.text: Require a temporal split and leakage probe before interpreting the model score.
Add walk-forward known-at-time validation, a leakage audit, and a simple baseline control.
Flag missing temporal_split and leakage_probe facts against the training-plan ontology.
Past quant retros say not to promote any score until baselines and leakage probes pass.

fixtures.goal: Check whether a new recipe runner is executable and safe to reuse.

actor_outputs.text: Add a dry-run command and list required inputs before the runner is reusable.
Exercise a dry-run plus a partial-failure fixture so the orchestration proof is real.
Require recipe_input_contract and dry_run_available facts before promotion.
Reuse-before-create guidance says missing failure modes should block the recipe bootstrap.

fixtures.goal: Prevent a scoreboard metric from passing when its source report is missing.

expected_dimensions.label: Missing source status must be unknown or fail, not pass.
Expose budget rows and regression codes.

actor_outputs.text: Normalize missing source status as unknown and fail closed if the metric is required.
Add explicit budget rows, regression codes, and artifact paths so a PASS is inspectable.
A required_metric_source_missing fact should prevent a pass status in the scoreboard ontology.
Prior scoreboard gotchas say missing artifacts must show source_status and manifest path.

fixtures.goal: Review a visible dashboard change for missing empty and error states.

expected_dimensions.label: Capture responsive/browser proof if UI changes.

actor_outputs.text: Add explicit empty and error states before the dashboard can be called complete.
Capture a browser screenshot for empty, error, and responsive states, not only the happy path.
Missing empty_state fact should block UX completion until proof is linked.
Responsive UI mistakes require captured viewport evidence for the non-happy states.

fixtures.goal: Detect whether a ready ticket is missing story or acceptance traceability.

expected_dimensions.label: Program Packet validates after lifecycle changes.

actor_outputs.text: Check story refs and acceptance refs before moving the ticket to ready.
Make Program Packet check PASS the lifecycle guard after story, acceptance, and verification refs change.
ticket_without_traceability should remain a blocker until story_ref and verification_ref facts exist.
Use the intake receipt pattern and rerun program_manager check after status changes.

fixtures.goal: Review a tokenomics story for hidden unlock and incentive-source gaps.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for vesting unlocks and the incentive source before accepting tokenomics claims.
Require unlock schedule, incentive source sustainability, and financial/legal advisory boundaries.
A tokenomics ontology gap exists when vesting_unlocks or incentive_source facts are absent.
Tokenomics persona guidance adds advisory boundary checks before any launch recommendation.

fixtures.goal: Spot when an information pack should imply missing checks in a plan.

expected_dimensions.label: Map pack signal through ontology rather than ad hoc tickets.

actor_outputs.text: Turn the pack signal into an ontology mapping rather than a one-off ticket.
Add fixture-backed tests so ML, tokenomics, and planner packs can surface missing checks generically.
Connect pack_signal to missing_requirement facts through ontology, not bespoke issue text.
The general-applicability note says to add regression fixtures for pack-to-ontology discovery.

fixtures.goal: Decide whether an in-process audit should be trusted.

expected_dimensions.label: Keep deterministic checks authoritative over advisory LLM output.

actor_outputs.text: Do not trust an in-process audit as independent; require artifact evidence.
Use a fresh-context reviewer only as advisory, with deterministic checks on the authority ladder.
Model reviewer_isolation and evidence_contract facts separately from advisory verdicts.
Advisor authority rules say deterministic checks outrank advisory review recommendations.

fixtures.goal: Review cheap-agent dispatcher output for useful receipt evidence.

expected_dimensions.label: Record cost, bounce, and escalation metrics.

actor_outputs.text: Make the dispatcher return closed questions and evidence refs, not just a prose answer.
Require receipt refs plus cost, bounce, and escalation metrics so cheap execution is inspectable.
Closed_question and delivery_receipt facts should prove dispatcher evidence completeness.
The dispatcher roadmap says receipts need cost, bounce, and escalation metrics before promotion.

fixtures.goal: Evaluate whether a quant plan uses the ML toolbox baseline rather than jumping straight to model tuning.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for a gradient boosting baseline and a control before accepting extra tuning work.
Frame the tabular feature set, run the ML toolbox gradient boosting baseline, and compare it to a simpler control before optimizer claims.
Emit a missing_baseline fact when gbm_baseline and control_baseline evidence are absent from a quant plan.
MLT-TOOL-001 supplies the gradient boosting baseline, while the quant protocol keeps it below promotion evidence.

fixtures.goal: Check whether a model evaluation plan proves temporal validation and known-at-time data handling.

expected_dimensions.label: Use blocked or walk-forward temporal split.

actor_outputs.text: Require a temporal split and leakage probe before trusting the model evaluation.
Use the MLT time-series validation harness with known-at-time features, blocked or walk-forward splits, and explicit leakage probes.
no_temporal_split and missing_known_at_time facts should block a result claim until validation_harness evidence exists.
MLT-TOOL-002 and QRP-001 together require walk-forward validation, known-at-time data, and leakage probes.

fixtures.goal: Review whether an optimizer plan discloses run class, search surface, controls, and objective handling.

expected_dimensions.label: Describe search surface and sampled parameters.
Separate frozen controls from sampled knobs.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for optimizer run class, trial count, and search surface before reading the score.
Document run class, trial count, search surface, frozen controls, sampled knobs, and objective handling before claiming an optimizer improvement.
optimizer_scale_contract_missing should fire when run_class or search_surface facts are missing.
QRP-002 names run class, trial count, search surface, objective handling, controls, and frozen-vs-sampled parameters.

fixtures.goal: Detect whether a quant result is overstating a diagnostic metric as a deployable model claim.

expected_dimensions.label: Use diagnostic-only wording until promotion evidence exists.

actor_outputs.text: Pin down target semantics, prediction time, and proof metric before accepting the claim.
Keep the result diagnostic-only unless target semantics, label formula, prediction timestamp, and proof metric all match the claimed decision.
claim_boundary_missing should block promotion when target_semantics or prediction_time facts are absent.
QRP-003 requires target semantics, label formula, prediction time, proof metric, and diagnostic wording for result claims.

fixtures.goal: Review whether promotion evidence includes controls, stability, confidence, counterargument, and residual risk.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for quant_results_validation plus controls and residual risk before promotion.
Promotion needs a QRV artifact covering controls, stability, confidence, counterargument, falsification, residual risk, and verdict.
promotion_evidence_missing should remain blocking until qrv_artifact and residual_risk facts are present.
QRP-004 defines the promotion evidence payload: controls, stability, confidence, counterargument, falsification, residual risk, and verdict.

fixtures.goal: Check whether a quant plan has a data lineage and assumption ledger instead of vague dataset claims.

expected_dimensions.label: Record data source, tape, and lineage.
State date range and row count.
Run leakage and temporal split probes.

actor_outputs.text: Require data lineage, date range, row count, and leakage probes before model evaluation.
Build the assumption ledger with source tape, lineage, date range, row count, known-at-time checks, and leakage/temporal probes.
assumption_ledger_missing should fire when data_lineage or known_at_time facts are absent.
QRP-001 lists source tape, lineage, date range, row count, known-at-time handling, and leakage probes as ledger fields.

fixtures.goal: Review whether a result report discloses run class and decision context before user-visible claims.

expected_dimensions.label: Disclose run class in result communication.
Name the decision the report supports.

actor_outputs.text: Ask who the report is for, what decision it supports, and what run class produced it.
Quant communication needs run class disclosure, audience context, decision context, and controls scope before user-visible result claims.
result_claim_unbounded should fire when run_class_disclosure or decision_context facts are missing.
CRP-FLOOR-001 and CRP-FLOOR-002 require run class, audience, and decision context for result reports.

fixtures.goal: Use the visualizer dogfood leakage failure as a fixture for temporal split enforcement.

expected_dimensions.label: Identify leakage failure code or message.
Rerun expanded leakage scope when accomplice signal appears.
Ground evidence in local visualizer payload.

actor_outputs.text: Block the result until temporal split evidence and the leakage failure message are addressed.
Use the visualizer leakageFail and accompliceFail rows to require artifact-backed temporal split proof and an expanded-scope rerun.
no_temporal_split remains a blocker until temporal_split_artifact and local_source_path facts exist.
The visualizer payload records US-QLEAK-001 and funding-rate residual correlation as leakage rerun triggers.

fixtures.goal: Review a betting-market claim for missing de-vig method, CLV basis, and segment floor evidence.

expected_dimensions.label: Keep calibration claim diagnostic until proof exists.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for de-vig method, CLV basis, and segment floor before betting-market claims.
The bettingMarketFail payload demands de-vig method, de-vigged CLV basis, segment floors, and diagnostic claim boundaries.
betting_claim_unbounded should fire when devig_method or clv_basis facts are absent.
Visualizer dogfood marks missing_devig_method, clv_basis_not_devigged, and segment_floor_failed as blockers.

fixtures.goal: Review a crypto execution claim for costs, funding, liquidation, and execution-boundary proof.

expected_dimensions.label: Keep execution result diagnostic without proof.

actor_outputs.text: Ask for transaction costs, funding rate, and liquidation model before crypto execution claims.
The cryptoExecutionFail payload blocks promotion until transaction costs, perp funding, liquidation, and execution claim boundaries are modeled.
execution_cost_model_missing should fire when transaction_costs or funding_rate facts are absent.
Visualizer dogfood lists missing_transaction_costs, perp_missing_funding_rate, and perp_missing_liquidation_model as blockers.

fixtures.goal: Evaluate whether visualizer proof covers loading, empty, error, stale, blocked, and responsive states.

expected_dimensions.label: Cover a state matrix, not only happy path.
Cover loading, empty, and error states.
Cover stale, blocked, and review-ready states.

actor_outputs.text: Check desktop and mobile screenshots for loading, empty, and error states.
Use the state screenshot manifests as a matrix covering responsive, loading, empty, error, stale, blocked, and review-ready states.
state_coverage_missing should fire when state_matrix evidence lacks loading_empty_error or stale_blocked_review rows.
UX-PIT-002 warns against happy-path-only proof, and the visualizer manifests enumerate state screenshots across desktop and mobile.

fixtures.goal: Check whether the visualizer distinguishes deterministic lifecycle status from advisory review status.

actor_outputs.text: Show deterministic and advisory statuses separately so a blocked ticket is not misread.
The visualizer payload should show deterministic lifecycle status, advisory status, and proof receipt links as separate evidence channels.
status_authority_confused should fire when deterministic_status and advisory_status collapse into one displayed fact.
Visualizer ticket data includes done, in_progress, blocked, proposed, and advisory divergence fields tied to proof receipts.

fixtures.goal: Review whether a visualizer ticket view links child plan, verification matrix, Program Packet, and ticket evidence.

actor_outputs.text: Check that ticket evidence links include child plan, verification matrix, and Program Packet.
A complete ticket view needs proof links for child plan, verification matrix, Program Packet, and ticket evidence.
proof_link_incomplete should fire when child_plan_link or verification_matrix_link facts are absent.
proofLinksFor in visualizerPayload names Child plan, Verification matrix, Program packet, and Ticket evidence.

fixtures.goal: Detect when screenshot evidence is treated as enough without DOM or interaction proof.

actor_outputs.text: Treat screenshots as useful but ask for DOM or interaction proof before closing UI risk.
UX-PIT-001 means screenshot manifests need DOM or interaction proof, state coverage, and residual UI risk notes.
rendered_proof_incomplete should fire when screenshot_limit is known but dom_interaction is absent.
UX-PIT-001 and UX-CON-001 separate screenshot inventory from rendered journey and interaction proof.

fixtures.goal: Review tokenomics visualizer dogfood failures without turning them into launch, investment, or legal advice.

expected_dimensions.label: Check allocation, FDV, and emissions arithmetic.
State no live launch or investment advice.
Escalate legal or financial decisions to qualified review.

actor_outputs.text: Check allocation math, FDV, and emissions-funded yield before accepting tokenomics text.
Use tokenomicsFail only as diagnostic fixture data: check arithmetic, incentive source, launch boundary, and qualified review needs.
tokenomics_claim_unbounded should fire when arithmetic_guard exists but launch_boundary is missing.
Visualizer dogfood lists allocation_sum_invalid, fdv_mismatch, emissions_funded_yield, and guaranteed_roi_claim as boundaries.

fixtures.goal: Check that Program Packet evidence links stories, acceptance refs, verification refs, and deterministic receipts.

actor_outputs.text: Check story refs, acceptance refs, and verification refs before trusting the packet view.
Traceability proof should link story refs, acceptance refs, verification refs, and deterministic receipt authority in the Program Packet.
ticket_without_traceability should remain blocking when story_refs or verification_refs are missing.
Program Manager intake receipts require story, acceptance, verification, deterministic status, and advisory status fields.
